# calcbloc: income tax tables and social security rates for R

calcbloc gives statisticians and economists tidy data frames of income tax
brackets, social security contribution rates, thresholds and allowances for
`r nrow(calcbloc::cb_countries())` countries, with the official source,
retrieval date and verification status on every row. National tables ship with
the package and work offline; regional tables and the latest revisions come
from the [CalcBloc public API](https://calcbloc.com/developers).

> **Status:** version 0.1.0, in review. Not on CRAN yet.

## Installation

```r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("itmarkerz/calcbloc-r")
```

calcbloc is pure R. It imports only [jsonlite](https://cran.r-project.org/package=jsonlite)
(JSON parsing) and [curl](https://cran.r-project.org/package=curl) (HTTP for the
optional API client), both available as binaries on every CRAN platform.

## What is in it

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| `cb_countries()` | Countries, tax years, regions and the date each was last verified |
| `cb_tax_table(country, year, region, source)` | A tidy data frame: one row per band or value, with `source_url`, `retrieved_at` and `status` |
| `cb_sections()` | The sections of a table (income tax bands, employee and employer contributions, ...) |
| `cb_tax_from_bands()`, `cb_band_breakdown()`, `cb_marginal_rate()` | Apply a progressive band schedule to a vector of incomes |
| `cb_manifest()`, `cb_regions()` | The dataset manifest and the regions with their own tables |
| `cb_net_salary()`, `cb_employer_cost()`, `cb_compare()` | Take-home pay, employer cost and two-country comparisons from the API |
| `cb_api_get()`, `cb_api_key()`, `cb_rate_limit()`, `cb_cache_clear()` | Low-level API access, key from `CALCBLOC_API_KEY`, quota status, session cache |
| `cb_credit()` | The credit line for plots and tables |

## Three examples

All output below is real, produced from the data bundled with this version.

### 1. US federal income tax brackets, applied to a vector of incomes

```{r}
library(calcbloc)

us <- cb_tax_table("us", 2026)
single <- us[us$section_id == "federal-income-tax-single", c("from", "to", "rate")]
single

income <- c(25000, 50000, 75000, 150000, 500000)
data.frame(income,
           tax = cb_tax_from_bands(income, us, "federal-income-tax-single"),
           marginal = cb_marginal_rate(income, us, "federal-income-tax-single"))
unique(us$source_url[us$section_id == "federal-income-tax-single"])
```

The tax on $75,000 matches the IRS rate schedule in Rev. Proc. 2025-32:
$5,800 plus 22% of the excess over $50,400.

### 2. Ireland's Universal Social Charge, band by band

```{r}
ie <- cb_tax_table("ireland")
usc <- cb_band_breakdown(50000, ie, "usc")
usc
sum(usc$tax)
```

EUR 1,032.82 is the figure in Revenue's own worked example (Sadhbh, EUR 50,000)
on [Calculating your USC](https://www.revenue.ie/en/jobs-and-pensions/usc/calculating-usc.aspx).
Note what the bands do not know: USC is not charged at all on incomes of
EUR 13,000 or less, a rule outside the band schedule.

### 3. The highest national band rate in every bundled country

```{r}
top_rates <- do.call(rbind, lapply(cb_countries()$country, function(cc) {
  tab <- cb_tax_table(cc)
  b <- tab[tab$kind == "bands" & tab$group == "income-tax" &
             !grepl("withholding|^pas-", tab$section_id), ]   # leave out withholding grids
  if (!nrow(b)) return(NULL)
  b <- b[b$rate == max(b$rate), ][1, ]
  data.frame(country = cc, currency = attr(tab, "currency"), section = b$section_id,
             top_rate = b$rate, from = b$from)
}))
top_rates[order(-top_rates$top_rate), ]
```

These are national (central government) schedules only. Where states,
provinces, regions, cantons or municipalities levy their own income tax (the
US, Canada, Spain, Switzerland and the Nordic countries, for example) it comes
on top, so the figures are not combined top rates. Germany is missing because
its tariff is a formula, published as single values; see
`cb_sections(cb_tax_table("germany"))`.

## Each row says where it comes from

```{r}
uk <- cb_tax_table("uk")
uk
str(as.data.frame(uk)[1, c("section", "label", "rate", "basis", "effective_from", "effective_to",
                            "source_title", "source_url", "retrieved_at", "status")])
```

## Online: regional tables and calculations

Regional tables (US states, Canadian provinces and territories, Scotland and
Wales, Spanish autonomous communities, Italian regions, Swiss cantons, Danish,
Swedish, Finnish and Portuguese regional rates) are fetched from the API:

```r
cb_regions("us")                                  # codes, offline
ca <- cb_tax_table("us", region = "ca", source = "api")
cb_countries(source = "api")                      # what the API serves today

# Calculation endpoints (about a dozen countries; free key recommended)
cb_net_salary("uk", 50000, region = "scotland")
cb_employer_cost("germany", 60000)
cb_compare("uk", "germany", 60000)
```

Without a key the API allows 50 requests a day and 5 a minute per IP address.
A free key from [calcbloc.com/developers](https://calcbloc.com/developers)
raises this to 5,000 a day; put it in `.Renviron` as `CALCBLOC_API_KEY=...` and
`cb_api_key()` picks it up. The client keeps at least a second between
requests, caches responses for the session, waits for `Retry-After` when the
server asks it to (up to `getOption("calcbloc.max_wait", 60)` seconds) and
reports the remaining quota with `cb_rate_limit()`.

## Coverage

Bundled national tables, from the package manifest
(data of `r cb_manifest()$generatedAt`):

```{r, echo = FALSE}
cs <- cb_countries()
cov <- data.frame(
  Country = sprintf("[%s](%s)", cs$name, cs$page_url),
  Code = sprintf("`%s`", cs$country),
  `Tax years` = cs$years,
  `Regional tables (API)` = ifelse(cs$regions > 0, as.character(cs$regions), "-"),
  Rows = cs$rows,
  `Last verified` = format(cs$last_verified),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(cov[order(cs$name), ], row.names = FALSE)
```

## Data, licence and credit

The tax data comes from the CalcBloc open dataset at
[calcbloc.com/data](https://calcbloc.com/data): every figure is taken from the
official government publication named next to it (`source_url`), with the date
it was retrieved and its verification status. Tables whose overall status is
`unverified` contain figures still being checked; filter on `status` if you
need verified rows only.

- **Data licence:** CC BY 4.0. Credit "Data by CalcBloc (calcbloc.com/data)"
  wherever you publish the data or results based on it; `cb_credit()` returns
  the text, for example `labs(caption = cb_credit())`.
- **Code licence:** MIT.
- Not tax advice: the band helpers apply the published schedule and nothing
  else (no allowances, credits, tapers or rounding rules).

To cite the package: `citation("calcbloc")`.
